Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

This is the right direction (the reused metadata budget and the silent five-minute floor are exactly what today's `finalize:plugins` / `post-update-plugins` reports look like on slow hosts), and the settlement evidence in the body is good. One finding from a diff-only review of `3f7464f82`:

**Git acquisition loses its deadline without gaining a cancellation path** (`src/infra/git-source.ts` around line 33). With no explicit timeout, `workTimeoutMs` becomes `null` and clone/checkout receive `timeoutMs: undefined`, but `acquireGitSource` accepts no cancellation signal and the command wrapper passes none to `runCommandWithTimeout`. A stalled `git clone` therefore has neither the finite deadline it had before nor a caller-controlled way to stop it, so the acquisition and its child can stay pending for the life of the process. The npm and archive paths in the diff carry the work policy with cancellation; Git needs the same: thread the signal through `acquireGitSource` and await child termination before deadline-free work is allowed there. A test that actually cancels a stalled Git child and asserts it is settled would close the gap (the current command tests check the forwarded timeout values only).

Everything else I looked for holds: explicit deadlines are honored without the floor, metadata checks keep their bounded budget, and the outer update budget still caps the phase. With the Git cancellation path in place this is landable.
